configurePresets.name: release-tests
configurePresets.description: Release build with the C++ tests enabled. Shares build/release with the 'release' preset ON PURPOSE: the release workflow packages out of build/release, so both presets must produce the executable at the same path. Re-running one preset over the other's tree only flips CODEHARBOR_BUILD_TESTS and reconfigures; it never leaves a stale binary behind.

configurePresets.name: mobile-desktop
configurePresets.displayName: Mobile shell on the workstation (Debug, both clients)
configurePresets.description: Builds the desktop client AND the mobile client (src/vt, src/mobile, codeharbor_mobile) for this workstation. This is how the mobile shell is developed and validated: it is plain Qt Quick with no device-only API, so it runs on a Linux/macOS/Windows desktop, and its tst_* targets run headless in the ordinary ctest suite. An NDK or an iPhone is needed to SHIP the mobile client, never to compile or test it.

configurePresets.name: mobile-base
configurePresets.description: Shared cross-compile settings for the Android and iOS clients. Qt ships no WebEngine for either platform, so the desktop client is off; the mobile presets do not build the web bundles either, because src/qml is never added. Tests are off because every tst_* target is a host executable that ctest would have to run, and a cross-compiled one cannot run here. CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH carries two entries: the Qt-for-<platform> prefix and CH_LIBSSH_PREFIX, the per-ABI libssh built from the in-tree vcpkg overlay (packaging/vcpkg-ports). An unset CH_LIBSSH_PREFIX degrades to the documented CH_HAVE_LIBSSH=0 warning rather than a configure error.

configurePresets.name: android-base
configurePresets.description: Shared Android cross-compile settings. Two entries here look redundant and are not, because this configure chainloads the NDK's own android.toolchain.cmake rather than Qt's qt.toolchain.cmake (which is what CH_LIBSSH_PREFIX-on-CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH buys us): the NDK toolchain sets neither. ANDROID_SDK_ROOT must exist as a CMAKE variable, not just an environment variable - Qt's deployment-settings generation globs <sdk>/build-tools/* out of that variable at CONFIGURE time and aborts with 'Could not locate Android SDK build tools' when it is empty. ANDROID_STL must be c++_shared because that is what Qt for Android itself is built against and what androiddeployqt bundles (libc++_shared.so); the NDK toolchain defaults to c++_static, which would put a second C++ runtime in the same process.

configurePresets.name: android-arm64
configurePresets.description: Release APK/AAB for 64-bit ARM devices. Needs ANDROID_NDK_ROOT, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, QT_HOST_PATH (the host Qt, for moc/rcc/qmlcachegen) and QT_ANDROID_PATH (the Qt-for-Android prefix, e.g. .../6.10.0/android_arm64_v8a). API 28 is Qt 6.10's floor.

configurePresets.name: android-arm64-debug
configurePresets.description: Same toolchain as android-arm64 but a Debug build, in its own binary directory so a debuggable APK and a release APK can coexist.

configurePresets.name: ios-base
configurePresets.description: Xcode, not Ninja: Qt's iOS deployment, bundle assembly and code signing are all driven through Xcode build settings, and a single-config Ninja tree cannot express the per-configuration SDK the simulator needs.

configurePresets.name: ios-arm64
configurePresets.description: Device build. Signing is deliberately left to the machine that runs it: set the development team through Xcode or -DCMAKE_XCODE_ATTRIBUTE_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<id>, so no team identifier is baked into the repository.

configurePresets.name: ios-simulator
configurePresets.description: Simulator build for Apple Silicon hosts. Code signing is turned off outright: the simulator does not check it, and requiring it would make an unsigned CI machine unable to compile the client at all.
